note: Plan: answers for a person who says they feel anxious, stressed or low. Only what a public-domain source says is used, each with its quote, source and licence. Food is never said to treat or calm anxiety, and no supplement is suggested. A doctor must sign this file before production (production refuses it). Sources are US public-domain pages from the National Institute of Mental Health; an Indian source (for example the Tele-MANAS programme page) can be added by the reviewer.

wellbeing.opening: I'm sorry you're feeling this way. Many people feel anxious, stressed or low at times, and it's good that you said so.

facts.text: Eating healthy, regular meals is one of the everyday habits recommended when you feel stressed or anxious.
facts.quote: Exercise, and make sure you are eating healthy, regular meals.
facts.source: National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH), 'I'm So Stressed Out! Fact Sheet'
facts.licence: Public domain: NIMH states the publication may be reused or copied without permission, with NIMH cited as the source.

facts.text: It is best to avoid drinking too much caffeine, such as coffee or soft drinks.
facts.quote: Avoid drinking excess caffeine such as soft drinks or coffee.
facts.source: National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH), 'I'm So Stressed Out! Fact Sheet'
facts.licence: Public domain: NIMH states the publication may be reused or copied without permission, with NIMH cited as the source.

facts.text: A regular sleep routine and enough sleep also matter.
facts.quote: Stick to a sleep routine, and make sure you are getting enough sleep.
facts.source: National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH), 'I'm So Stressed Out! Fact Sheet'
facts.licence: Public domain: NIMH states the publication may be reused or copied without permission, with NIMH cited as the source.

wellbeing.limits: Food can't treat anxiety, so I won't suggest a special food or a supplement for it.
wellbeing.help: If you are struggling to cope, or the feelings won't go away, please talk to a doctor or a counsellor. You can also call Tele-MANAS on 14416 (free, any time, in many Indian languages).
wellbeing.urgent: If you have chest pain or trouble breathing, or you feel you might harm yourself, call 112 now.
wellbeing.bridge: If you'd like, I can help with meals that fit the programme.
